title: Multi-region: Postgres vs CockroachDB
brief: An app runs in two regions, 4k requests/s, 90% reads. Side A keeps one Postgres primary (plus a replica) in us-east-1, so us-west-2 crosses the country for every query. Side B runs CockroachDB across 3 regions with 5 replicas. Decide which you'd run, for which requirements.

scenarios.label: us-east-1 goes down
scenarios.about: At 10 s the whole us-east-1 region fails, for 20 s. Postgres's primary lives there.
scenarios.watch: At 10 s us-east-1 goes down for 20 s. Watch the errors number: the Postgres primary is in that region, so its writes fail. CockroachDB keeps a quorum in the other regions.

scenarios.label: Steady 4k rps
scenarios.about: Nothing fails. Postgres pays cross-region latency for every west request; CockroachDB pays a quorum round trip on writes.
scenarios.watch: Nothing fails. Watch p99: Postgres pays a cross-region hop for every us-west request; CockroachDB pays a quorum round trip on writes.

questions: What does surviving a region loss cost, in $/hr and in write latency?
If the business accepts 20 minutes of downtime a year, which would you run?
How would you cut Postgres's cross-region read latency without changing databases?
Which side is simpler to operate, and does that matter here?
hints: Which requests cross a region border on each side, and how often?
Postgres: every us-west-2 request goes to us-east-1 (+70 ms). CockroachDB: reads stay local, writes wait for a majority of replicas in other regions.

CockroachDB survives the region loss and has lower p99 here, for ~25% more. Postgres is cheaper and simpler; a read replica in us-west-2 would fix its reads, but a region loss still takes writes down until you fail over.
_notes: Two graphs: client -> lb -> api-east / api-west (8 x 1k each, in their regions) -> db. Postgres (primary + 1 replica, 3k/node estimate) is inside us-east-1: west requests add 70 ms (cross-region estimate). CockroachDB sits outside the region boxes (it spans 3 regions): 5 nodes x 3k, replication factor 5, reads local, writes + 70 ms quorum averaged over the write share (the sim adds the mean, so p99 understates write latency). Sim steady: p99 156 vs 73 ms, $2.08 vs $2.55/hr. Region down 10-30 s: Postgres dies with us-east-1 (errors 40.8% over the run, recovers 22 s after the failure = when the region is back); CockroachDB keeps serving through us-west-2 (8 replicas take 4k at rho 0.5). Not modeled: failover to a Postgres replica, consistency anomalies. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
